newsitem.title: USA: Vanguard chief says equity markets too speculative.
newsitem.headline: Vanguard chief says equity markets too speculative.

text.p: The chairman of the Vanguard Group of mutual funds said Friday that trade in the U.S. equity markets is currently too speculative.
"The concerns are that we are selling in the market on much more of a speculative basis than an investment basis," John Bogle said in an interview on the Cable News Network (CNN) program Moneyline."
"I think there is too much speculation in this market," he said.
However, he said he has not advised clients to book profits, but rather to hold steady.

"We are getting (clients) emotionally ready for a decline that may come, but we are not telling them to act on their emotions now by selling. Nor are we telling them to jump in when it goes down. It's pretty much stay the course," Bogle said.

When asked what could trip the market's spectacular run, Bogle said a rise in inflation, which could precipitate an interest rate increase by the U.S. Federal Reserve, or simply a change in investor sentiment.

"Perhaps most importantly of all, investors could just, for one reason or another known to nobody in the world, just decide their expectations are too high. And markets sell today particularly on high expectations," he said.
The Vanguard Group has some $300 billion under management, CNN said.
On Wednesday, the Dow Jones Industrial Average closed above the 8000 milestone for the first time.
